blocks.text: Sergius Paulus. The proconsul of Cyprus who "believed" at Paphos.
“The deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to…”
ROME: 17 RULERS HEROD THE GREAT → PORCIUS FESTUS
"The deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God." Acts 13:7
Elymas the sorcerer withstood them, "seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith". Acts 13:8
"Then the deputy, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord." Acts 13:12
Where Paul and Barnabas found him
At Salamis Barnabas and Saul "preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews". Acts 13:5
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE · PUBLISHED BY CESNOLA
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE · COPIED 1912; LETTERS OF ABOUT AD 60-100
None. Acts gives no year for the visit to Cyprus.
Ramsay dates the first journey from spring 47; this dates Paul's visit, not the length of the proconsulship.
Possibly: some of the family leaned toward Christianity

From inscriptions of the family at Pisidian Antioch, Ramsay asks whether the proconsul and his daughter Sergia Paulla were "either Christian or half-way on the road towards Christianity" while other relatives stayed pagan. Acts 13:12 [21]
No member of the family is known to have been Christian
Dessau, the editor of the register of Roman officials, wrote that "evidently no member of this family was Christian"; Ramsay agreed for the family's well-known members.[21]
Acts says nothing of Sergius Paulus after Paul and Barnabas left Paphos.
Acts does not say that he was baptized.
Acts gives no year and no length for his proconsulship.

Scholars' viewThe King James "deputy" stands for the Greek title of a proconsul, the governor of a province under the senate. Lightfoot (1889) shows from Dio Cassius and the inscriptions that Cyprus was then governed by proconsuls, so the title Luke uses is the right one. Acts 13:7 [13]
